questions.stem: About chemical synapses:
options: The neurotransmitter diffuses from the presynaptic to the postsynaptic element through gap junctions
The pre- and postsynaptic membranes are continuous
questions.explanation: No official answer key for this exam — answers worked out from the course.

questions.stem: The routes of neurotransmitter elimination are:
questions.explanation: No official key — reuptake is presynaptic (and glial).

questions.stem: In an electrical synapse, synaptic transmission is carried by:
Postsynaptic potentials recorded at neuro-neuronal synapses are phenomena that are:
options: Reflecting conductance changes at the presynaptic level

questions.stem: In a neuro-neuronal synapse:
options: The neurotransmitter is not always acetylcholine
Sodium entry into the presynaptic terminal causes neurotransmitter release
The neurotransmitter can cause depolarization of the postsynaptic element
The neurotransmitter can cause hyperpolarization of the postsynaptic element
questions.explanation: No official key — calcium entry triggers release.

questions.stem: Assisted (mediated) membrane transport:
options: Is defined as primary active when it depends on ATP hydrolysis
Follows the electrochemical gradient if it is passive

questions.stem: The end-plate potential (EPP) physiologically reflects:
options: An electrotonic depolarization of the presynaptic membrane
A local depolarization of the postsynaptic membrane
An interaction between acetylcholine and nicotine

questions.stem: Which signaling pathway allows ligands to act at a distance?
Cell-surface receptors can be:
In the cAMP pathway, the G protein stimulates:
When a ligand binds a G-protein-coupled receptor, the G protein can:
options: Trigger the formation of second messengers
Trigger the opening of an ion channel
questions.explanation: No official key — kinases are activated by second messengers, not directly by the G protein.

questions.stem: The resting membrane potential is mainly determined by:
Conduction of the action potential in myelinated fibers:
options: Is slower than in unmyelinated fibers
Is faster than in unmyelinated fibers

questions.stem: Which substance blocks sodium channels?
questions.explanation: No official key — TEA blocks K⁺ channels.

questions.stem: In skeletal striated muscle:
options: Thick filaments are mainly made of myosin molecules
The sarcomere is the contractile functional unit
Each muscle fiber receives several nerve terminals from one motor neuron
The heads of actin contain the binding sites for myosin
questions.explanation: No official key — each fiber receives a single terminal.

questions.stem: Myosin is:
options: Made of 2 heavy chains and one light chain
Made of 2 heavy chains and 4 light chains
Its head contains an ATP hydrolysis site
questions.explanation: No official key — the head binds actin and ATP.

questions.stem: The thin filament: actin is
options: Made of 2 light chains and 2 heavy chains
Made of G-actin, troponin and tropomyosin
Contraction is the sliding of thin filaments between thick filaments

questions.stem: During contraction:
options: ATP is needed for contraction but not for muscle relaxation
ATP resynthesis occurs only through oxygen-consuming mechanisms
The resting length is the length of the muscle in the body at rest
The heat produced during shortening is proportional to the force

questions.stem: At the neuromuscular junction:
options: Acetylcholine release is triggered by the arrival of the motor neuron action potential
The duration of action of acetylcholine is not limited
The end-plate potential is a local potential, gradable by spatial and temporal summation
Transmission can be blocked by curare

questions.stem: Concerning skeletal muscle metabolism, the energy used comes from:
options: Direct phosphorylation of ATP by creatine phosphate

questions.stem: Chemical energy is stored in the form of:
questions.explanation: No official key — the store is creatine phosphate, not creatinine.

questions.stem: The regulatory center of the autonomic nervous system:
options: Does not exist; it is autonomous

questions.stem: Dry mouth is due to:
Muscarinic receptors are found in:
The adrenal medulla:
options: Is a gland with a catabolic effect
Releases small amounts of noradrenaline and adrenaline at rest
questions.explanation: No official key — it is a modified sympathetic ganglion.

questions.stem: The internal environment (milieu intérieur) is:
options: Interstitial fluid makes up most of the internal environment
It represents 2/3 of total body water volume
questions.explanation: No official key — ECF is 1/3 of total body water.

questions.stem: All these fluids make up the internal environment except:
Plasma osmolarity is:
options: Identical to that of interstitial fluid
Identical to that of intracellular fluid

questions.stem: Concerning the tracer dilution method:
options: The tracer must diffuse into all fluid compartments
Tritium (³H) is the tracer used to measure total body water volume
It is the reference method for measuring body fluid volumes
The tracer must be strongly eliminated and/or metabolized
questions.explanation: No official key — the tracer must diffuse only into the compartment measured and be little eliminated.

questions.stem: The mechanisms of interstitial edema can be:
The Gibbs–Donnan law governs ion concentrations and distribution in the body's compartments:
options: [Na⁺] of extracellular fluid is higher than [Na⁺] of intracellular fluid
Plasma protein concentration is lower than that of the interstitial fluid
[K⁺] of intracellular fluid is higher than [K⁺] of extracellular fluid
[Cl⁻] of extracellular fluid is lower than [Cl⁻] of intracellular fluid

questions.stem: Concerning water balance anomalies, the consequences of a positive water balance are:
The thermal neutrality zone:
options: Varies from one species to another
Is the temperature corresponding to basal metabolism
Is the body temperature at which no thermoregulatory response is engaged
questions.explanation: No official key — it is an ambient temperature range, not a body temperature.

questions.stem: Food calorimetry:
options: Allowed definition of the caloric equivalent of the different substrates
Has an imprecision factor: the digestive factor

questions.stem: Extra heat (specific dynamic action) is greatest for:
The Berthelot bomb calorimeter measures:
options: The theoretical caloric value of organic matter
The real caloric value of organic matter
The caloric value after partial combustion of organic matter
The caloric value after total combustion of organic matter

questions.stem: The food ration is defined as:
options: The amount of food needed to cover an individual's weekly needs in matter and energy
The amount of food needed to cover the daily needs of a group of individuals in matter and energy
The amount of food needed to cover an individual's daily needs in vitamins and ATP
The amount of food needed to cover an individual's daily needs in matter and energy
